# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS (TASK-031 STEP 2)
#   The gate measured sandbox_linux.go at 41/134 (30.6%) and the question was WHY.
#   A diagnosis that lives only in a task report cannot be re-checked by whoever
#   implements the fix, so the raw evidence is committed here.
#
#   THIS IS AN EXTRACT, NOT THE WHOLE PROFILE. The runner profile is ~507KB covering
#   the entire repo; only the sandbox_linux.go blocks are reproduced below, because
#   they are the ones the diagnosis turns on. The full artifact is retrievable from
#   the run URL above while the retention window lasts.
#
# THE FINDING: FIVE FUNCTIONS SIT AT EXACTLY ZERO, AND THEY PROVABLY EXECUTED.
#   applyLandlock and applySeccomp DEMONSTRABLY RAN on this very host — the sandbox
#   installed and held, and the previous run's EINVAL diagnostic was raised from
#   inside applyLandlock. A function that provably executed and reports 0/29 is a
#   MEASUREMENT failure, not an untested-code failure.
#
#   The mechanism: these five run inside the re-exec helper, which ends in
#   unix.Exec (sandbox_linux.go). exec REPLACES THE PROCESS IMAGE, so Go never
#   flushes the helper's coverage counters. The counters are lying, not the code.
#
# THE DECISIVE ARITHMETIC
#   79 of 134 statements are structurally unmeasurable under the current producer.
#   Even 100% coverage of every remaining statement caps this file at 55/134 = 41.0%,
#   which is less than half the 90% floor. NO conventional test can make this file
#   green. That is what rules out the naive form of the "just write more tests" fork.
#
